From the moment I stepped into Kolapasi Indian Canteen, I was greeted with such warmth and a cozy, family‑style atmosphere—truly felt like home. Their South Indian fare is incomparable—authentic, flavorful, and lovingly handmade. They offer generous samplings of every dish so you can make an informed choice—think of it as an Indian version of Chipotle, but with so much more soul.

Every item is made from scratch—no artificial colors, no MSG, no shortcuts—just pure, honest cooking. And the highlight: the tender coconut payasam—creamy, fragrant, and absolutely divine!

Kolapasi Chapel Hill brings fast‑casual dining up a notch, blending heartfelt service with high‑quality ingredients. A true gem—I’ll be back soon!

The setup is similar to Chipotle, but with authentic South Indian dishes that taste like they came straight from someone's home kitchen. Everything is flavorful, comforting, and made with care.

Lots of amazing vegetarian options, too—nothing feels like an afterthought. This place truly shines when it comes to both food and service.

Bonus: they’re socially responsible, which makes supporting them feel even better. Highly recommend checking it out!

Kolapasi Indian Canteen just opened up in St. Augustine at World Golf Village.
170 Registry Blvd Ste 103.
If you’re a fan of authentic South Indian food, this place is a must-try!

Fun fact: Kolapasi means hungry in South India — and trust me, you’ll want to come hungry because the menu is loaded with bold, crave-worthy dishes. Everything is made from scratch with fresh ingredients, and you can taste the difference in every bite.

The setup is pretty cool too — you actually get to see the food before you decide, and you can build your own bowl with endless combinations. From classic curries like Butter Chicken, Chettinad Chicken Curry, and Dal Tadka, to specialties like Goat Roast, Kerala Beef Fry, Nilgiri Chicken, and Spicy Coconut Chicken — the flavors are spot on.

They also have plenty of rice options (Lemon Rice, Coconut Rice, Biriyani Rice, and more) plus flaky layered parottas that are perfect for soaking up all that curry goodness.

And don’t skip dessert — the Beetroot Halwa, Tender Coconut Payasam, and Mango Lassi are the perfect way to end the meal.

Whether you’re in the mood for biryani, curries, or just want to build a hearty custom bowl, Kolapasi is bringing South Indian comfort food straight to St. Augustine. I’ll definitely be back to explore more of their menu!

I ordered one butter chicken for pickup two fays ago; first impression when I got there was the place was nice and the man behind the counter was very friendly, I was pretty excited given the good reviews and I'd been trying Indian food from all the restaurants in the area recently. The order came quickly and I didn't have to wait, however, once I got home I opened the container and it was the most soupy, watery butter chicken I had ever seen. The flavors were just not right and it had an almost orange-grey color to it... it was maybe the worst butter chicken ever. It felt as though when I asked for it mild they just poured a cup of water and mixed it in to do so.

Maybe it was a fluke, just bad luck, or an accident in the kitchen, but as it stands I cannot recommend anyone eat that butter chicken that I had. I wish I had taken a picture to add to the review.

EDIT: I went back and spoke with one of the co-owners about the menu and tried the butter chicken again as well as a few other menu items. Overall it was a vast improvement from my first visit and greatly improved my opinion of the establishment. I will say the butter chicken was still uniquely different than what I normally expect from an Indian restaurant, less creamy than I would have liked, but the flavors and experience was much better this go around and the other menu items were great! I particularly enjoyed the KP chicken and ghee rice combination. The parotta was delicious as well.

This small but cute indian restaurant totally surprised me in the best way. The first thing you notice is the cute color combo in the decor — bright, fun, and just a really happy vibe overall. The inside is nicely decorated, spaced out well, and feels super welcoming.

But the coolest part? They actually let you taste their menu items. Like… as many as you want. I’ve been to plenty of Indian restaurants, and this is the first time I’ve seen that. Love the confidence.

We tried the ghee rice, chicken chukka, and goat ghee roast, and every single dish was packed with flavor. And I have to mention their parotta — because wow. Around the Jacksonville/St. Augustine area, most places serve parotta/paratha that tastes just like the frozen ones from the store. But not here. This one was flaky, soft, and genuinely delicious… the real deal.

The food overall took me straight back to my years in Chennai — the spices and flavors were spot on. Plus, most of their meat dishes are boneless, which is always a nice bonus.

Portion sizes are great, everything was tasty, and overall it was a super solid experience. Kolapasi is definitely worth checking out if you’re anywhere near St. Augustine.
